body:
When HDR2D is off, these effects are all blended in sRGB space. When HDR2D is on, these effects are blended in linear space. 

I think moving glow to linear space is probably a change we can make. But for adjustments, I think we are just going to have to document the difference and live with it. I don't think it is possible, or even desirable to try to make them behave the same when HDR2D is on and off. 

Ultimately, we need to do a better job at communicating the fact that games need to be designed with HDR2D in mind. It isn't a setting that should be flipped on and off at run time, or for different users. Your art pipeline needs to consider it, so it should be a fixed decision from a project point of view

Although brightness, contrast, and saturation are entirely subjective and can be performed in either linear or sRGB encoding (if ignoring the impact on future HDR output), both banding (dithering) and color correction effects were designed to be applied on sRGB encoded values and are incorrect when applied to linear encoded values (when HDR 2D is enabled). ~~The middle screenshot shows this issue.~~

Edit: I've removed references to Color Correction from this report and created a separate issue instead: #107730

I prefer to not change behaviour in any way (logic, visuals, etc.) unless there is a very strong reason to do so or it is a major release (i.e. 5.0). For this reason, I do not think it is a good idea right now with the current state of Godot to change the behaviour of Glow, BCS, and HDR 2D when many projects have been tuned to the specific existing behaviour.

But in relation to the 5.0 release and HDR output support, I believe there is value in having a clear understanding of what is correct and desirable behaviour and what is not.

> But for adjustments, I think we are just going to have to document the difference and live with it. I don't think it is possible, or even desirable to try to make them behave the same when HDR2D is on and off.

Considering the framing for discussion I just shared, I am confused by why it would not be possible or even desirable to make them behave the same when HDR2D is on and off. Isn’t this simply a mater of ordering in the tonemapping shader?

> Ultimately, we need to do a better job at communicating the fact that games need to be designed with HDR2D in mind. It isn't a setting that should be flipped on and off at run time, or for different users. Your art pipeline needs to consider it, so it should be a fixed decision from a project point of view

I’m not sure if this is true for the upcoming HDR output PR: I expect that most users who are developing a 3D game would want to have HDR 2D disabled for SDR version of their game for performance reasons and also allow players to optionally enable HDR output support. In this scenario, the difference in 3D Adjustments behaviour makes it difficult to author the game. Or is there no performance benefit to having HDR 2D disabled? Or maybe it’s impractical to support both modes in one game because 2D GUI stuff of a 3D game will be very different, even though no Adjustments were applied?

I get the feeling that there might be some major fundamental things that I don’t quite understand? This is something that I would like to get a good understanding of, especially in relation to HDR output, tonemapping, effects, etc. I’m happy to discuss here or have a voice call or chat during the rendering meeting if that’s easier.

> Considering the framing for discussion I just shared, I am confused by why it would not be possible or even desirable to make them behave the same when HDR2D is on and off. Isn’t this simply a mater of ordering in the tonemapping shader?

Perhaps, I guess when using HDR2D we could convert to sRGB, apply color correction and adjustments, then convert back to Linear. That would require all of our tonemappers to be reversible (I don't think Filmic is reversible though, and maybe not ACES or AGX either). 

The fundamental problem is that the output of the tonemapping shader is either Rec 2020 (when using 2DHDR) or it is tonemapped sRGB otherwise. Color correction and adjustments are placed at the end of the shader after tonemapping and sRGB conversion. However, if using HDR2D, tonemapping and sRGB conversion happen when blitting to the swapchain _after_ rendering 2D. Therefore, we can't apply color correction and adjustments both _after_ tonemapping and _before_ 2D rendering. And we don't want to apply color correction to 2D elements

> I’m not sure if this is true for the upcoming HDR output PR: I expect that most users who are developing a 3D game would want to have HDR 2D disabled for SDR version of their game for performance reasons and also allow players to optionally enable HDR output support.

The difference is mostly for 2D content. Your 2D content will look different depending on whether HDR2D is enabled or not. If all of your 2D content is opaque it won't have much of an impact. But anything that is blended will look different because blending in sRGB vs linear space makes a big difference. I don't think it is realistic for anyone who cares about their art pipeline to release a game that supports HDR2D on and off.

That isn't to say that HDR output can't be toggled. But if you want the ability to support HDR monitors, then you need to design your game with HDR2D in mind. 

> Or is there no performance benefit to having HDR 2D disabled? 

On desktop devices and current flagship mobile devices there is no performance benefit to disabling HDR2D. On older mobile devices and low end mobile devices there may be a performance benefit to disabling HDR2D depending on the scene content and the particular device. 

> Or maybe it’s impractical to support both modes in one game because 2D GUI stuff of a 3D game will be very different, even though no Adjustments were applied?

Yes, the big difference is from blending of semi-transparent 2D objects.
